elements.element: Customer has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation.
elements.evidence: Rendered 6.1 replaces the covenant entirely: "HDI shall be a non-exclusive provider of the services under this Agreement, and the Company shall have no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation to HDI." The original prohibition on the Company participating "in any project similar to the Site ... with respect to Deerskin Products" is deleted, and so is HDI's "exclusive right to use of the 'Deerskin' brand," so no exclusive Vendor right remains to block Customer's use of its own brand. Deterministic scan "no requirements/sole-supplier obligation on Customer remains" returned ok.

elements.element: Exclusivity is limited to a defined product category.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: after the edit no exclusivity obligation binds the Company at all, so there is no scope to confine to a product category. The stated condition (an existing exclusivity covenant) does not apply.

elements.element: Exclusivity lasts no longer than 12 months.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: the full-term covenant tied to the auto-renewing term under Section 4.1 is removed, so no exclusivity period runs at all.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet service levels.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no exclusivity survives that would require a service-level exit trigger.

elements.element: Exclusivity ends automatically if Vendor fails to meet delivery dates.
elements.evidence: Vacuously satisfied: no exclusivity survives that would require a delivery-date exit trigger.

reasons: Finding status "deviation" is correct: original Section 6.1 barred the Company from any similar Internet project for Deerskin Products for the whole auto-renewing term with no performance-based exit, and additionally granted HDI an exclusive right in the Company's own "Deerskin" brand — walk-away territory, well short of the fallback (category-limited, 12 months, automatic exit on service-level/delivery failure).

Preferred level is position-complete: both halves of the offending sentence (the Company's negative covenant and HDI's exclusive brand right) are excised in the same operation, and the replacement states affirmatively that the Company has no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation. Nothing is left merely promised in the comment.

Minimality holds: the edit is confined to the single exclusivity sentence in Section 6.1. HDI's reciprocal covenant in Section 6.3 and the non-exclusive Marks licence in the following paragraph of 6.1 are untouched, and no survival tail, expense, remedy or procedural boilerplate is added. The dropped opening words "Except as provided in Section 6.2" were part of the deleted covenant, so their removal is necessary rather than cosmetic. The paired formulations ("non-exclusive provider" / "no exclusivity or sole-supplier obligation") are two facets of the same single element rather than a duplicated operative term, so this does not fail the duplication test, though the drafter could tighten to the second limb alone if HDI objects to belt-and-braces phrasing.

Intent is preserved: pricing, term, Section 1.6 launch-stage termination, the Section 4.2 Termination Payment and the Marks licence all survive without contradiction, and no remaining sentence reimposes exclusivity.

Housekeeping to confirm (not an element failure): Section 6.2 was drafted as a carve-out from the deleted covenant. Verify that 6.2 does not now read as an orphan "Notwithstanding Section 6.1" exception or reintroduce any restriction on the Company's other Internet projects; if it does, conform or delete the stranded cross-reference in the same operation so no undefined or contradictory retained sentence is left.
